styles.name: 纸感手写笔记

styles.desc: 把一个东西拆开，一步一步演示里面怎么运转。
styles.fit: 抓公告那个例子（定时、抓取、筛选、总结、提醒），讲"它到底是怎么做到的"。
styles.prompt: 做一段动态图形，讲清楚 [东西] 是怎么工作的。把过程拆成 [3 到 5] 步，每一步一个画面，前一步的结果变成下一步的开头，最后合起来看全貌。

styles.name: 配方式步骤
styles.desc: 像做鸡尾酒教程，从空杯子开始，每加一样东西就标出名字和分量，最后成品。
styles.fit: "你只要这几步就能做出一个小工具"这种教学段落。
styles.prompt: 用讲解视频的风格，从 [起点] 一步步做到 [成品]。每加入一样东西，画面上同时标出它叫什么、加了多少。[N] 秒。

styles.name: 五幕讲解（万能讲解模板）
styles.desc: 五个画面讲完一件事。
styles.fit: 一期科普的骨架，或者感受线里讲一个工具的段落。
styles.prompt: 你是一个资深动态设计师。用一个 HTML 页面做一段 [30] 秒的讲解动画，分 5 幕：1）观众遇到的问题；2）[东西] 是什么；3）怎么用，3 步；4）一个真实的例子；5）结尾卡片写 [频道名]。字要大要粗，转场要顺，用我们的配色。

styles.name: 四段式发布片
styles.desc: 大环境、痛点、解决办法、好处，四段，最后 logo 动画收尾。
styles.fit: 介绍一个新工具、一个 skill 的段落。
styles.prompt: 你是一个资深动态设计师。做一段 [30] 秒的视频，4 到 5 个场景：为什么现在这件事重要、大家现在的麻烦、[工具] 怎么解决、用了以后的好处。文字逐词出现，用弹簧物理做动作，元素踩着节拍进场，不要突然冒出来。每出现一个元素配一个很轻的音效，其他时候安静。最后用 logo 动画加一句话收尾。做完自己渲染出来逐帧检查，有重叠、被裁掉、太赶的地方改好再给我。

styles.name: 口播 + 逐字字幕
styles.category: 情绪和氛围类（感受线最常用）
styles.desc: 白底，一种字体，字幕跟着说话一个词一个词打出来，配真实的图片，镜头慢慢漂。
styles.fit: 全片的主线。有人讲解、口播的片子，字幕必须对上。
styles.prompt: 以口播录音为主线。字幕跟着说话逐词出现，时间用 Whisper 从录音里对出来，不按文案逐字对。白底，只用一种字体，黑字。镜头每段只做一次慢慢的漂移。图片在音乐的 16 分音符上换。屏幕上的字不要句号。不要给字加选中框一样的底色。音乐在关键那句话上起来，人声出来的时候音乐自动压低。响度统一到 -14 LUFS。

styles.name: 情绪弧线：混乱、掌控、清晰
styles.category: 情绪和氛围类（感受线最常用）
styles.desc: 全片一条弧线。开头画面乱，中间慢慢理顺，最后干干净净落在一句话上。转场靠同一个形状变过去，不硬切。
styles.prompt: 全片是一条连续的弧线：从混乱，到掌控，到清晰，最后落到 [结尾那句话]。场景之间用同一个物体、同一个形状变过去，不要硬切，除非有特别的理由。动作要有高级的缓动和错开的层次，有一点景深和光感。不要满屏模糊、不要弹来弹去的界面、不要粒子。每一个重要的画面单独截出来都能当海报用。

styles.name: 把一个抽象概念、一种情绪做成画面
styles.category: 情绪和氛围类（感受线最常用）
styles.desc: 没有具体的人和物，用形状、文字、颜色的变化表现一种感觉。
styles.fit: 讲恐惧、焦虑、不安、"想太多"这种情绪的段落。
styles.prompt: 做一段 [15] 秒的动态图形，表现"[情绪/概念]"这个感觉，比如"焦虑"、"对未知的恐惧"。不要具体的人和物，用形状、文字和颜色的变化来表现。从 [一种状态] 慢慢变到 [另一种状态]。

styles.name: 人生循环
styles.category: 情绪和氛围类（感受线最常用）
styles.desc: 同一个人从小到老，最后无缝接回开头。
styles.fit: "学无止境"、"一直在学"这种讲长时间的段落。
styles.prompt: 做一段 [20] 秒的动画，同一个人从 [阶段1] 到 [阶段2] 到 [阶段3]……最后无缝接回开头，可以循环播放。

styles.name: 剪纸皮影
styles.category: 情绪和氛围类（感受线最常用）
styles.desc: 纸剪的剪影在光后面演戏，配轻轻的声音。
styles.fit: 讲"家"、讲回忆、讲温暖的段落。竖屏很合适。
styles.prompt: 用纯 JavaScript 做一段 [30 到 60] 秒的竖屏 9:16 动画，剪纸皮影戏的风格。配轻柔合适的声音，声音也用代码做。主题是：[一个问题，比如"是什么让一个地方变成家"]。

styles.name: 手绘定格，第一人称
styles.category: 情绪和氛围类（感受线最常用）
styles.desc: 手绘的、一帧一帧有点抖的定格动画，画面里的东西自己开口说话。
styles.fit: 让一个东西替你说话。比如让"那个抓公告的小工具"自己介绍自己。
styles.prompt: 做一段手绘定格动画。你就是 [东西]，用第一人称跟观众介绍你自己。

styles.name: 无对白短片，声音讲一半
styles.category: 情绪和氛围类（感受线最常用）
styles.desc: 没有台词，全靠画面和声音讲故事。
styles.fit: 片头、片尾，或者两段之间的过渡小片段。
styles.prompt: 做一个 [45] 秒的无对白短片，声音要讲出一半的故事。故事你来编，主题是 [主题]。

styles.name: 对称暖色的电影感空镜
styles.category: 情绪和氛围类（感受线最常用）
styles.desc: 画面左右对称，粉嫩暖色，像一个精致的小舞台。比如火车窗外四季流过，桌上一杯咖啡。
styles.fit: 讲时间流逝、讲停下来想一想的段落。比如"停播这段时间"。
styles.prompt: 火车窗外四季流过，车厢很温暖，桌上放着一杯咖啡。画面左右对称，粉嫩暖色，像精致的舞台布景，镜头很稳。

styles.name: 日落天空的 3D 空镜加一句话
styles.category: 情绪和氛围类（感受线最常用）
styles.desc: 3D 场景，日落、紫色的云、海面反光，镜头慢慢飞，画面上写一句短话。
styles.fit: 情绪最高的那一句话，比如"现在不就是最好的时候吗"。
styles.prompt: 用网页 3D 做一个日落的海面，紫色积云、海面反光，镜头像动画电影那样慢慢飞过去。画面上写一句：[一句话]。

styles.name: 东方意境
styles.category: 情绪和氛围类（感受线最常用）
styles.desc: 古典诗词里的画面，比如月夜、江水、楼阁，可以配可交互的网页。
styles.fit: 讲心境、讲文化的段落，也适合做片头。
styles.prompt: 根据你对我的了解，选一个我可能喜欢的东方古典意境（比如月夜、江水、楼阁），做一个 [30] 秒的视频，再做一个可以交互的网页版。

styles.name: 粘土定格 MV
styles.category: 情绪和氛围类（感受线最常用）
styles.desc: 粘土小人一帧一帧动，手作感很强。
styles.fit: 轻松、好玩的段落；你自己的歌也可以做成这种 MV。
styles.prompt: 做一个 [60] 秒的粘土定格动画风格的音乐视频，粘土小人有手指印和手作质感，动作一顿一顿的。顺便写一首适合这个画面的原创歌。

styles.name: 文字建筑（口播金句专用）
styles.desc: 只用文字。每个词有一个"结构上的角色"：有的是梁，有的是柱子，有的是地板。前面的词搭起来，最后一句话"站"在前面搭好的东西上。
styles.fit: 结尾金句"学习，相信自己"。全片最值得做的一段。
styles.prompt: 做一段 [20] 秒、只用文字的口播动画。台词按顺序是：[第1句]、[第2句]……每个关键词有一个结构上的角色，比如"学习"是地基，"相信"是柱子，"自己"是站在上面的人。文字用真实的字形轮廓搭出来，每一句都改变画面的结构。最后一句必须"站"在前面那些词搭好的东西上。配色：深色背景、纸色字、一个强调色。不要麦克风、人群、旗子这类俗套画面，不要素材视频。做完挑 8 帧检查，读起来顺序对，最后的平台确实是前面的元素搭起来的。

styles.name: 歌词卡点
styles.desc: 歌词跟着人声和节拍一个字一个字跳出来。
styles.fit: 你自己的歌，或者片子里有一段唱的部分。
styles.prompt: 根据附上的歌做一个歌词动态视频，歌词和动画要和人声、节拍完全对上。

styles.name: 破框
styles.desc: 一张海报里的东西冲出了海报的边框。
styles.fit: "跳出原来的想法"、"不再觉得跟我没关系"这种转折。
styles.prompt: 做一段动态设计：一张海报里的 [东西] 冲出海报自己的边框。

styles.name: 一个元素串全片
styles.category: 结构和镜头类（用来把不同风格串起来）
styles.desc: 一个小东西（一个橙色圆点、一个白球）贯穿所有场景：它先是开关，再变成字母上的点，再变成曲线，再变成一个图形，最后回到结尾。
styles.fit: 混搭风格时的"线"。比如可以用一个小圆点代表"公告"、代表"想法"，从头跟到尾。
styles.prompt: 一个 [颜色] 小圆点串起每一个场景：[场景1里它是什么]，然后变成 [场景2里的什么]……最后回到结尾卡片。圆点不能瞬移，只能连续地动过去。动作干脆利落，弹簧回弹很小，没有空档。不用素材视频、渐变、发光、粒子爆炸、随机转场。最后一帧和第一帧一样，可以循环。

styles.name: 一镜到底
styles.category: 结构和镜头类（用来把不同风格串起来）
styles.desc: 从头到尾不切镜头，每个场景都是从上一个场景里"长"出来的。
styles.fit: 讲变化的段落，比如"以前要自己推，现在坐进去它自己走"，一个画面变到另一个画面。
styles.prompt: 一镜到底。每个场景都从上一个场景里变出来：文字从一条线里升起来，按钮展开成页面，用一种颜色铺满画面切到下一段。不要淡入淡出、不要模糊、不要硬切。每个场景镜头只做一次缓动。

styles.name: 从一个点拉远到宇宙
styles.category: 结构和镜头类（用来把不同风格串起来）
styles.desc: 黑屏上一个点，慢慢展开成画面，再一直拉远，整个桌面变成太空里的一个点，再推进到另一个画面。
styles.fit: 讲尺度、讲"从一个小工具到一个系统"。
styles.prompt: 从黑屏上的一个点开始，展开成 [画面]，镜头在好几个尺度上推拉，一直拉远到整个画面像太空里的一个点，再推进到 [另一个画面]，最后落到 [一句话]。

styles.name: 一个形状变到底
styles.category: 结构和镜头类（用来把不同风格串起来）
styles.desc: 同一个形状不停变：按钮、加载圈、播放器、滑块、开关……每次变都是鼠标真的点了一下。
styles.fit: 一口气列很多例子的段落，比如"整理表格、写周报、批量改文件、做自媒体"。
styles.prompt: 一个形状从头到尾不切，依次变成 [例子1、例子2、例子3……]，变的是大小、圆角和颜色。每次变化都由鼠标真的点击或拖动触发。到处用弹簧，最多一点点回弹。镜头跟着放大，让每个状态填满画面。最后一帧和第一帧一样。

styles.name: Logo 慢慢拼出来（片头片尾）
styles.category: 结构和镜头类（用来把不同风格串起来）
styles.desc: 碎片慢慢聚拢，拼成 logo。
styles.fit: 每期的片头或片尾，做一次以后反复用。
styles.prompt: 做一段慢慢揭示的转场：碎片一点点聚拢，最后拼出你的 logo。

styles.name: 苹果发布会风
styles.desc: 柔和、白、亮蓝、玻璃质感，镜头从不停在静止画面上切。
styles.fit: 展示工具、展示界面的段落。
styles.prompt: 苹果发布会的感觉：柔和、白、亮蓝、玻璃质感。镜头从不在静止画面上切，每个镜头进来时已经在动，离开时加速或者带运动模糊。字体用 Inter。不要出现紫色、品红和橙色。

styles.name: 极简卡点
styles.desc: 一个镜头只讲一件事，大量留白，只用一个强调色，每一刀都在重拍上。
styles.fit: 节奏快的段落，比如"你每天要整理的表格、你每周要写的周报……"。
styles.prompt: 高级极简。一个镜头只讲一件事，大量留白，只用一个强调色，字距收紧的无衬线字体，文字用遮罩显出来，镜头稳。每一刀都切在重拍上，每个界面动作踩在拍子上。屏幕上的字不要句号。不要冲击波、粒子、RGB 分离、抖动、光晕、霓虹、闪烁、弹来弹去的缓动。只用可以商用的音乐和音效。

styles.name: 竖屏快节奏 POV
styles.desc: 竖屏，节奏很快、很碎，第一人称视角，动作和音效都很满。
styles.fit: 竖屏版的开头 3 秒，抓住人。
styles.prompt: 竖屏 9:16，快节奏碎剪，第一人称视角，讲 [主题]，动作和音效都要做得很好，加一点你自己的性格。

styles.name: 新闻快讯盘点

styles.fit: 以后做"这周 AI 圈有什么新东西"这种盘点。
styles.prompt: 做一个约 60 秒、好看好懂的动态图形，像新闻快讯那样介绍 [时间段] 里 [领域] 的新东西，从普通用户的角度说清楚每一条有意思在哪。

styles.prompt:
# Caption News — Style Prompt

> Social-video news that reads with the sound off. Real footage, photos and the source document are the ground; huge captions are the lead actor, slammed in a chunk at a time with one keyword on a yellow block. Hard cuts on a music grid, numbers that roll, a source tag that slides in whenever a figure appears, and the original document highlighted on screen before its number is believed. 16:9, built for a feed.
> References (grammar only): the captions-first social news of the mid-2010s (NowThis, AJ+), horizontal explainers that set big type over footage (Bloomberg Quicktake). Never copy their logos, fonts, colour ratios, idents or shots, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: 1920 年代新闻片
styles.desc: 1926 年报纸说查尔斯顿会跳坏膝盖，福特工人野餐会上的孩子照跳不误。
styles.prompt:
# 1920s Newsreel — Style Prompt

> A sound newsreel of the late 1920s, cut from real archive material: a searchlight-and-globe ident with a brass fanfare, a newspaper that spins into the lens, a fast and cheerful announcer on an optical soundtrack, place-and-date cards, maps, magazine pages and documents, wipes, flips and irises, and a hot band that can stop dead for the punchline.
> References (grammar only): **Fox Movietone News** and **Universal Newspaper Newsreel** (1927–1930s) — the ident ritual, the announcer's patter, one story per location, the stinger after the last story; **Pathé News** — the item title card; Hollywood's **spinning newspaper** montage; **1920s hot dance bands** (Charleston rhythm, banjo, tuba). Never copy a real newsreel's name, logo, globe design, typeface or fanfare.

styles.name: 倒计时分屏
styles.desc: 阿尔忒弥斯二号发射的最后一分钟，一秒不剪：格子从 1 开到 9，点火合成 1。
styles.fit: 对比、倒计时，比如"三个月"
styles.prompt:
# Live Countdown Split-screen — Style Prompt

> An edit style, not a look. Real footage of one event with a known zero (a launch, a verdict, a final whistle, polls closing), shown in real time: screen time equals event time, a clock ticks every second, and the screen splits into more and more cells as the moment nears, every cell showing the same second. At zero the cells merge into one picture and the clock flips.
> References (grammar only): the real-time clock and splitting screens of the TV series *24*; the multi-camera archive panels and mission-time codes of the documentary *Apollo 11* (2019). Never copy their type, colours, sounds, graphics or shots, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: 延时摄影交响
styles.desc: 纽约的一天：延时光河、踩着十六分音符的网格，1899 年和今天并排。
styles.prompt:
# Time-lapse Symphony — Style Prompt

> A city film cut like a piece of minimalist music: time-lapse turns traffic, crowds and clouds into rivers of light, the cuts get denser with the score's subdivisions, one thing is slowed almost to a stop, and the film ends on a hard cut to black on a downbeat. No narrator. The music carries it.
> Grammar learned from the city-symphony tradition and the "Qatsi" films (Reggio / Fricke, scores in the Philip Glass manner). Nothing is taken from those films: no footage, no melody, no title lettering, no names in the film.

styles.name: 视觉调查
styles.desc: 新闻片、照片、证词和调查报告排上同一条时间轴，五路来源指向一处。
styles.fit: 几个来源对到一条时间线上，科普里讲来龙去脉
styles.prompt:
# Visual Investigation — Style Prompt

> A cold investigation desk: footage, photographs, documents, sound and maps from one real event, laid out on one shared clock so they check each other. The clock lives inside the picture — timestamps on the evidence, a playhead on a data chart, a stopwatch over the decisive seconds; frozen frames are circled and magnified; quotes are highlighted on the page they come from; a plan shows where cameras stood and where they looked; what is known and what is not are kept apart; at the end every piece of evidence is pulled into one map.
> References (grammar only): newspaper visual-investigation videos, forensic-architecture reconstructions, broadcast verification units. Never copy them, quote their names or use their branding.

styles.name: 构成主义蒙太奇
styles.desc: 帝国大厦的小册子写着建造者，工地实拍和老照片给出答案：每天 2,500 人。
styles.prompt:
# Constructivist Montage — Style Prompt

> Real archive footage, photographs and documents, printed as one ink-and-paper poster with a single red, and cut on a machine beat. Diagonal bands carry the type; windows cut along the axis hold the film; people are scissored out of photographs and stacked into structures; numbers count, documents are marked in red, and two images collide to make a third idea.
> References (grammar only): Soviet montage cinema of the 1920s (city symphonies with split screens, counting and machine rhythm; "intellectual" montage where A + B yields a concept), constructivist posters and photomontage (red / black / paper, steep diagonals, photo cut-outs with geometric blocks, type as structure). Never copy their shots, layouts, slogans or lettering, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: 体育战术板
styles.desc: 半场 0–3，费内巴切 12 分钟连进三球：冻住画面、画线、分屏、射门图。
styles.fit: 定格、画线讲解，拆一个瞬间
styles.prompt:
# Sports Telestrator — Style Prompt

> The TV football analysis segment: play the clip at full speed, rewind, freeze it, and draw on the broadcast picture — rings under players' feet, marker arrows for the ball, a red patch for the space nobody covered — then play on, switch angles, count the frames, and flatten the pitch into a board. Real match footage is the ground; every line is drawn on top of it and moves with it. A studio show's packaging (sting, corner bug, score bar, a yellow wipe) holds it together. 16:9.
> References (grammar only): touch-screen analysis segments in televised football (the "telestrator" pundit's board), and explainer channels that annotate real match footage. Never copy a broadcaster's or channel's logo, fonts, colours, idents or graphics, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: 电视新闻包装
styles.desc: 一周四条 AI 新闻，一整套电视台包装：串联单、标题条、翻牌价格表、规格卡。
styles.prompt:
# Broadcast News Package — Style Prompt

> A television newsroom's on-air package, built entirely in code: a sting that becomes the channel bug, a rundown of today's stories that opens and closes the bulletin, a lower-third strap that never leaves the bottom of the frame, and full-frame graphics (split-flap price boards, a line breaking a threshold, explainer maps, documents flying out of a city, quote cards, spec cards with proportion bars, stamps) that carry the facts. The style is the **package system plus its cutting rules**, not a drawing style. 16:9, a clean frame: no burned-in subtitles, no news crawl.
> References (grammar only): evening network news headline menus, financial-channel market graphics, European news channels' explainer maps, tech-desk spec cards. Never copy a broadcaster's logo, set, fonts, colours, music or idents, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: 卫星地图简报
styles.desc: 卫星照着地图去找咸海，找到的是沙漠；只有筑了坝的那一块回来了。
styles.prompt:
# Satellite Briefing — Style Prompt

> Real satellite imagery of a real place, graded down to an analyst's grey, with thin white measurement lines drawn on the ground: a lock-on reticle, outlines, a range line, one reading. One continuous zoom built from stacked imagery plates carries the viewer from orbit to the ground and back, and time can run inside one locked frame.
> References (grammar only): open-source investigation films that annotate satellite pictures (thin lines on imagery, one claim per screen, measuring as the plot); the Eameses' *Powers of Ten* (one continuous change of scale with a readout); NASA Earth Observatory's *World of Change* (one place, time running). Copy none of their layouts, typefaces, icons or music; never name them in the film.

styles.name: 工程方案比较墙
styles.desc: 一条河要架桥，四种桥型在一面简报墙上逐个受检，拍板的是桥下要过的船。
styles.prompt:
# Engineering Briefing Board — Style Prompt

> One real whiteboard wall, filmed: window light on enamel, ghosts of erased marker, frame and tray. Cut-out photographs of real things land on it with weight; tags, magnets, a ruler and stamps are pinned to it; marker ink draws itself in three colours with fixed meanings. The camera rides the lines from fact to fact and only at the end pulls back to show the whole briefing.
> References (grammar only): explainers filmed on a map wall; the long pull-back over a wall covered in work; drafting conventions (plan above elevation, dimension lines, hatching). Never copy them or name them in the film.

styles.name: 激光点云扫描
styles.desc: 激光点云剥掉一片森林的树冠，露出当年农田的石墙：3.4 公里。
styles.prompt:
# LiDAR Survey — Style Prompt

> Real airborne laser points of a real place, floating in the dark as a measured cloud; a scan line or a cutting plane passes through them and the points condense into a solid, raking-lit surface, which is then measured with hairline instruments. One designed camera move carries the whole film: the cloud is something you fly through, not a picture you look at.
> References (grammar only): survey and archaeology lidar visualisations (colour as height, the canopy removed); architectural section drawings (a cut, dimensioned); museum film cadence (one held reading per screen). Copy none of their layouts, ramps, typefaces or music, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: 白模投影
styles.desc: 投影机把数据一层层刷上鹿特丹白模：从 1940 年的空洞到今天的塔楼。
styles.fit: 把数据投到白色模型上
styles.prompt:
# Projection on White Model — Style Prompt

> A pure white massing model of a real place stands on a plinth in a dark room, and a projector paints data onto it as light: one layer at a time, falling on the surfaces that face it, spilling a little past the plate. The model never changes; only the light on it does.
> References (grammar only): projection-mapped planning models in city galleries (the dark room, the soft throw, colour only on white surfaces); macro model photography (shallow focus at rooftop height); editorial data graphics (one figure, one label, one source per layer). Copy none of their layouts, typefaces, colours or music, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: 数据实体化
styles.desc: 十二年风电和太阳能装机叠成实物，绕表盘升成两条螺旋，2021 年太阳能反超。
styles.prompt:
# Data Physicalization — Style Prompt

> Real statistics built as real objects: every unit is a countable piece of material (a plate, a block, a coin, a bar) stacked to exact scale on a crafted base, shot like a product in a studio — soft key, long shadows, shallow depth of field, physically based materials. The camera reads a number at the edge of one plate, follows the data as it grows, and pulls back until the chart is an installation.
> References (grammar only): data-sculpture and physical-visualisation practice (one unit = one object, the object is the axis); product and still-life photography (a warm key at a low angle, a cool rim, a seamless sweep); annual-report editorial design (one reading per screen, a source line, a quiet grotesk). Copy none of them; never name them in the film.

styles.name: 爆炸图拆解
styles.desc: 开源键盘的一半在一次环绕中逐层拆开，看到主控再合拢，标上真实尺寸。
styles.fit: 拆开看里面，比如 AI 由哪几部分组成
styles.prompt:
# Exploded Teardown — Style Prompt

> A real product, built from its own engineering files (CAD, PCB layout, bill of materials), lit like a studio packshot and taken apart in front of the camera: the layers lift on one axis, the camera travels between them, every part is named with the numbers its files contain, and it closes again into one object.
> References (grammar only): hardware-launch exploded films (layer stagger, orbit timing), repair-guide teardowns (opening order, the macro on the part that matters), engineering drawing (leaders, dimension lines). Never copy their products, layouts, typefaces or music, or name them in the film.

styles.name: 显微镜故事
styles.desc: 一镜从肝组织玻片推到单个细胞核，两个圆逐像素数出 2.4 倍的蓝。
styles.fit: 一层层放大，讲眼睛、神经这类感知科普很合适
styles.prompt:
# Microscope Story — Style Prompt

> Real, licence-clean microscopy of a real specimen, seen as it is, and one continuous change of scale that carries the viewer from the glass slide in the hand to a single cell. Focus breathes when the magnification changes, a focal plane sweeps when the camera lands, and every scale bar, field of view and reading comes from the image's own metadata.
> References (grammar only): Charles and Ray Eames' *Powers of Ten* (one continuous change of scale with a readout riding along); premium microscope launch films (dark bench, glass catching light, restrained marks, clean instrument sound); digital-pathology viewers' instruments (scale bar, field of view, magnification). Copy none of their layouts, interfaces, typefaces or music; never name them in the film.

styles.name: 档案灯箱
styles.desc: 电报说最长飞了 57 秒；放大镜下，莱特兄弟的底片和档案说是 59 秒。
styles.prompt:
# Archive Light Table — Style Prompt

> Real archive objects (glass negatives, slides, letters, telegrams, clippings, drawings) lie on a cool, backlit light table. A loupe comes down on one of them, and inside the glass the object comes alive: a negative turns positive, a line of type lights up, a number lifts off the page, a photograph opens into depth. Precise catalogue numbers, dates and readings are pinned to the objects. Clean, modern and quiet, with no vintage filter.
> References (grammar only): archive documentaries that push into still photographs; visual investigations that annotate real imagery (one line, one reading, one source per screen); product macro films (glass edges, transmitted light). Copy none of their layouts, typefaces, shots or music, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: 蜡笔儿童绘本
styles.desc: 月亮失眠了，小女孩爬上屋顶给它唱摇篮曲。
styles.prompt:
# Crayon Picture Book — Style Prompt

> A picture-book page drawn live in wax crayon on toothy paper, with a watercolour wash that reveals what the crayon was hiding.
> References (grammar only): Raymond Briggs' *The Snowman* (1982) (hand-textured frames that breathe, wordless tenderness, a lyrical passage carried by one tune, still backgrounds with living figures). Copy none of its characters, song or imagery, and never name it in the film.

styles.name: 水彩笔刷

styles.prompt:
# Watercolor Brush — Style Prompt

> A hand-painted journal page that paints itself: translucent brush strokes with dry-brush flying white on warm cotton paper, hand-written notes beside what is painted, nothing drawn with a vector line.
> References (grammar only): naturalist field-journal and botanical-plate watercolours (specimen + note); long horizontal handscroll panoramas (one continuous painted world); the textbook "transect" diagram (a gradient read across space). Borrow the grammar, never a specific artwork, character or layout.

styles.name: 中国水墨

# Chinese Ink Wash — Style Prompt

> Xieyi ink painting on rice paper, animated: blank paper is space, one brushstroke is a mountain, a wave, a gesture or a cut.
> References (grammar only): Shanghai Animation Film Studio's *Feelings of Mountains and Water* (1988) (blank-paper space, ink bloom, guqin pacing, figures in a few strokes); the bamboo-forest fight of *Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon* (weightlessness, stillness before action). Copy none of their characters, compositions or music.

styles.name: 油画厚涂

styles.prompt:
# Impasto · Palette Knife — Style Prompt

> Thick oil paint laid with a palette knife: big, flat, sharp-edged planes of colour, raked by light so every ridge of paint shows. Clarity first: value structure before texture, hard edges at the focus, calm planes everywhere else.
> References (grammar only): the opening titles of *The Umbrellas of Cherbourg* (1964) (overhead choreography read as moving colour); palette-knife street paintings (Leonid Afremov and the genre around him) (knife mosaic, vertical wet reflections, warm lights against cool shadow); Sorolla / Sargent (few, decisive strokes and strong light); Edgar Wright's music-locked editing (one action, one sound, one cut). Never copy their images, compositions, melodies or characters, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: 一笔画
styles.desc: 一根不离纸的线画完一个人的一生，再把笔交给孩子。
styles.fit: 一条线讲到底，和样片库 C2、M4 一起看
styles.prompt:
# One-line Drawing — Style Prompt

> A single ink line that never leaves the paper. Everything on screen is that one line being drawn; scenes don't cut, they morph.
> References (grammar only): Osvaldo Cavandoli's *La Linea* (1971) — one line is both the world and the character, and transformations of the line are the jokes and the transitions; Gjon Mili's 1949 photographs of Picasso drawing with light — the confidence and speed of a single gesture; Norman McLaren's *Begone Dull Care* and *Boogie-Doodle* — lines drawn *to* the music. Do not copy La Linea's character, its gibberish voice, or any specific continuous-line illustration.

styles.name: 白板讲解
styles.desc: 手机怎么知道你在哪：GPS、原子钟，和相对论每天多出的 38 微秒。
styles.fit: 讲道理、讲步骤，就是你发来的那条
styles.prompt:
# Whiteboard Explainer — Style Prompt

> An explainer drawn live on one glossy dry-erase board: single-line handwriting that is actually *written* stroke by stroke, floating markers with no hand, magnets that can move, an eraser that can rewind, and a camera that travels across the board instead of cutting.
> References (grammar only): RSA Animate / Cognitive Media (one continuous board, the camera travels instead of cutting, a full-board view); minutephysics (one sentence = one drawing, the simplest geometry that carries the idea); Steve Reich's *Piano Phase* (two copies of one figure at two tempi as a structure). Never copy their drawings, characters, hands or music.

Suits explainers, usually science or "how does X work"; the length follows how many ideas the board has to hold.

styles.name: 钢笔淡彩
styles.desc: 公园只是一张钢笔速写，风把草帽吹到哪里，哪里才有颜色。
styles.prompt:
# Urban Sketch · Pen & Wash — Style Prompt

> A sketchbook page drawn on location: fine sepia fineliner lines that wobble, overshoot and never quite close, with loose transparent watercolour dropped on top. The colour sits slightly off the lines, spills over them, and dissolves into cream cold-press paper at the page edge.
> References (grammar only):
> - Urban-sketching sketchbook pages: line first, then wash; colour off-register; handwritten date and place in the corner; the page edge breaking up into dabs.
> - *Paperman* (2012): a monochrome world with one coloured object.
> - *The Red Balloon* (1956): an object as the protagonist, the camera following it across a city.
> - Jazz waltz (the Vince Guaraldi school): 3/4 swing, walking bass, brushes, a woodwind lead.
>
> Nothing is copied from these: no characters, melodies, layouts or type.

styles.name: 皮影戏
styles.desc: 十日炙烤大地，后羿张弓射日。
styles.fit: 讲故事，和 M12 一起看
styles.prompt:
# Shadow Puppetry — Style Prompt

> Chinese shadow theatre: translucent dyed-hide puppets, carved like lace, pressed against a cotton screen and lit from behind by oil lamps.
> References (grammar only): Lotte Reiniger's *The Adventures of Prince Achmed* (1926) for profile acting and lace-like scenery; Shaanxi / Huayin shadow theatre for carving, colour and gong-and-drum rhythm. Never reproduce a specific historical puppet, melody or recording, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: 浮世绘
styles.desc: 旅人走向远山，每个镜头都是一幅版画；巨浪是高潮，结尾是远山与整幅画轴拉远。
styles.prompt:
# Ukiyo-e — Style Prompt

> Edo-period woodblock prints brought to life: flat colour blocks, carved ink lines, bokashi skies, paper you can feel, and a camera that moves over the print like an unrolling handscroll.
> References (grammar only): Hokusai's *Thirty-six Views* (one constant subject placed differently each time; bold geometric cropping); Hiroshige's *Fifty-three Stations* and *Hundred Famous Views* (small figures, rain lines, extreme foreground framing); the anime *Mononoke* (2007) (print texture alive in motion, flat layers sliding, seals as screen language). Never reproduce a specific famous print (no copy of *The Great Wave*, *Red Fuji*, *Sudden Shower over Ōhashi*), and never copy their characters or compositions.

styles.name: 红色窗花剪纸
styles.desc: 除夕年兽进村，小女孩剪出的大窗花照亮全村，把它吓跑。
styles.prompt:
# Red Paper-cut — Style Prompt

> Chinese window-flower paper-cuts brought to life: jointed red cut-outs on paper grounds, where the cut *is* the drawing and the holes are where the light gets in.
> References (grammar only): folk window flowers of Shaanxi and Yuxian (sawtooth, crescent, cloud and swirl cuts, fold-symmetric rosettes, *yin* and *yang* cutting); the 1958–59 Shanghai Animation Film Studio cut-paper shorts (jointed figures, profile acting, paper layers in parallax). Copy no studio character, no named artist's work and no real motif sheet: generate every pattern from code, and never name the references in the film.

styles.name: 纸雕灯影
styles.desc: 一枚月饼讲中秋的团圆与思念，纸雕灯箱层层透光。
styles.prompt:
# Paper-cut Lightbox — Style Prompt

> A layered paper-cut shadow box (纸雕灯) lit from behind: 6–9 sheets of cut card stacked in a shallow box, a warm light glowing through the paper, windows and moons burning through holes, soft shadows falling from each layer onto the next. The frame is the box; the camera is a macro lens inside a lamp.
> References (grammar only): commercial paper-cut shadow-box lamps (纸雕灯 / "shadow box lightbox") for the layer stack and backlight; Lotte Reiniger's silhouette films for the cut-out, jointed figure language; Chinese 剪纸 motifs (auspicious clouds, eaves, mountains) as one possible vocabulary. Do not copy any specific lamp design, film frame or character.

styles.name: Risograph 丝网印刷
styles.desc: 周日早晨骑车穿过城市：面包店、公园、河边，每到一处加一版油墨，最后三版套印。
styles.prompt:
# Risograph Print — Style Prompt

> Animation that looks printed, frame by frame, on a stencil duplicator: two or three translucent spot inks overprinted on warm paper, halftone dots, ink grain, and plates that never quite line up.
> References (grammar only): Tom Haugomat's riso illustrations (colour fields and silhouettes, a small figure in a large world, extra colours made by overprinting); Jacques Tati's *Jour de fête* (comedy staged small in a wide frame, everyday sounds as rhythm); real riso prints (translucent inks, misregistration, pinholes, feed streaks). Copy none of their characters, compositions or palettes.

styles.name: 复古半调案卷
styles.desc: 橘猫胖橘被立案审查：测试重力、凌晨跑酷，最后无罪释放。
styles.prompt:
# Halftone Dossier — Style Prompt

> A retro print case file: cream archive paper, overprinted halftone dots in a few flat inks, huge heavy headlines with misregistered shadows, rubber stamps that slam, and thick-outlined characters. The film is a file that is read out one exhibit at a time.
> References (grammar only, never copy): Ben-Day-dot pop-art printing (Roy Lichtenstein era comics) for dot density as shading; riso/offset overprint zines for multiply layers and misregistration; police mugshot height charts and case-file folders for the framing device; Japanese variety-show telop captions for the keyword-highlight caption bar.

styles.name: 木刻版画
styles.desc: 村子用一整个冬天铸一口钟，钟声第一次响起，雪停了。
styles.prompt:
# Woodcut Print — Style Prompt

> A relief print that carves itself: every frame is a black wood block, and light only exists where a knife has cut it away. One colour at most, and only for the thing that burns.
> References (grammar only): Frans Masereel *Passionate Journey* (1919) and Lynd Ward *Gods' Man* (1929), wordless woodcut novels told as a sequence of self-contained plates; Käthe Kollwitz's woodcuts, where emotion lives in the direction of the gouge; Gustave Doré's engraving, where line spacing and direction build light and volume. Never copy their plates, figures, borders or titles.

styles.name: 铜版画
styles.desc: 一张博物志图版自己刻出来：雕刀推开铜版，蜜蜂一线线成形，最后手工水彩上色。
styles.prompt:
# Copperplate Engraving — Style Prompt

> An intaglio plate that engraves itself: a burin cuts swelling lines into copper, a proof is pulled, and the figure builds up — outline, hatching, cross-hatching — until engraved lettering, magnified details and a hand-laid wash make a finished plate.
> References (grammar only): 19th-century natural-history plates — Haeckel, Audubon, Westwood, the *Britannica* copperplates (centred subject, numbered roundels, roman title over an italic name, "del." / "sculp." credits, the plate mark); Hogarth and Doré for the burin line (hatching that follows the form, crossing only in half-tones); hand-coloured plates for washes laid after printing. Never copy a plate, pose, border or title.

styles.name: 丝印旅行海报
styles.desc: 三条步道各一张丝印海报，一色一刮印出来，再沿山脊一镜到底从正午爬到黄昏。
styles.prompt:
# Silkscreen Travel Poster — Style Prompt

> Opaque, hard-edged flat inks pulled one colour at a time through a screen: 4–6 inks per poster, stepped colour bands instead of gradients, thin paper-white gaps where the registration slips. Information is revealed the way the print is made: one layer, one beat.
> References (grammar only):
> - **1930s–40s WPA national-park screen prints**: 4–6 flat inks, lit and shade faces, stepped-band skies, a dark information band, concentric sun rings.
> - **Fifty-Nine Parks (contemporary)**: restraint, paper as a colour, a series on one template with a new palette per poster.
> - **The physical process**: hinged screen, squeegee pushing an ink bead across mesh, split-fountain pulls, drag streaks, pinholes, off-register slivers.
>
> Never copy a real poster's composition, park name, lettering or logo, and never name a real agency.

A **scene style**: it does a practical job (a guide, an event poster, a destination series) for any place, event or product with a few facts. See §11 for the jobs.

styles.name: 瑞士动态排版
styles.desc: 一张音乐会海报按瑞士设计的五条规则自己排版，第五条是只打破一条。
styles.prompt:
# Swiss Motion Graphics — Style Prompt

> International Typographic Style in motion: a modular grid, one typeface, one signal colour, and movement as exact as a printing press.
> References (grammar only): 1950s–70s Zurich posters (Müller-Brockmann, Hofmann, Gerstner, Crouwel) for the grid, flush-left type, scale contrast and "designing programmes"; modern identity systems in motion (Experimental Jetset, Pentagram) for snaps on the beat. Never copy a specific historical poster's composition (no concentric-circle or fan layouts lifted from Müller-Brockmann), never use Helvetica or Akzidenz font files, never name a real institution on a poster.

styles.name: 60s 间谍片头
styles.desc: 虚构 1964 年间谍片的片头：追一把被偷的钥匙，几何碎片最后拼成片名。
styles.prompt:
# 60s Spy Title Sequence — Style Prompt

> A cut-paper, four-ink opening title sequence for a film that never existed: silhouettes move through sets built out of the credits themselves, every brass stab is a cut, and a title is assembled from the pieces.
> References (grammar only): Saul Bass's titles for *North by Northwest*, *Anatomy of a Murder* and *Vertigo* (flat opaque inks, abstraction down to silhouettes, type as structure); the 2002 homage by Kuntzel + Deygas for *Catch Me If You Can* (a cut-paper chase through graphic sets, lateral tracking). Not a gun-barrel opening, not a tiptoeing cartoon panther, not a copy of any real title's logo, lettering, characters or shots.

styles.name: 装饰艺术
styles.desc: 1930 年的大饭店，门童赶在午夜前把一封信送上顶楼。
styles.prompt:
# Art Deco — Style Prompt

> Black lacquer, engraved gold line and airbrushed geometry: a 1930s poster that moves. Every composition has a centre axis, transitions open or close along it, and light arrives as bulbs switching on one by one.
> References (grammar only): **A. M. Cassandre** posters (giant geometry, steep perspective, airbrush inside hard edges); **Chrysler Building / Rockefeller Center ornament** (setbacks, sunbursts, chevrons); **Busby Berkeley** overhead numbers overheads (human kaleidoscopes); **The Great Gatsby (2013) title sequence** (gold line drawing itself on black); **Gershwin-era symphonic jazz** (clarinet, piano, muted trumpet). Never copy a poster layout, a real building, a character, a typeface design or a melody.

styles.name: 蓝图 / 工程制图
styles.desc: 发明家的蓝图自己画出一台接云机器，修订云线变成了真的雨云。
styles.prompt:
# Blueprint — Style Prompt

> Engineering drawings that come alive on a sheet of cyanotype paper: white technical line work on Prussian blue, drawn in drafting order, with annotations that move.
> References (grammar only, never copy): the moving technical drawings in Prologue Films' *Iron Man* (2008) end credits, Leonardo's *Codex Atlanticus* pages, 19th-century US patent drawings (Fig. 1 / Fig. 2, part balloons, fine-line shading), the automaton drawings in *Hugo* (2011). No Marvel elements, no real patents, no real inventor's machine or signature.

Suits films of 30–60 s.

styles.name: 彩色玻璃窗
styles.desc: 阳光从清晨移到黄昏，照到哪一格花窗，哪一格的故事就动起来。
styles.prompt:
# Stained Glass — Style Prompt

> A medieval stained-glass window seen from inside a dark stone hall, alive only where the sun touches it: light is the clock, the camera and the story.
> References (grammar only): the window prologue of *Beauty and the Beast* (1991) (chapters pane by pane, a storyteller's pace); the glass knight of *Young Sherlock Holmes* (1985) (glass that cracks and recombines piece by piece); 12th–13th-century Chartres glass (colour logic, grisaille, leading). Copy none of their characters, compositions, subjects or music.

styles.name: 象形运动图形
styles.desc: 2026 亚运会 43 个大项，几何象形人卡着节拍快闪。
styles.fit: 小图标卡点，讲步骤、讲数字
styles.prompt:
# Pictogram Motion — Style Prompt

> A beat-locked flash-card film built from three things only: a **square-grid "core graphic"** of circles, half-discs and tiny patterned cells whose rows slide past each other; **geometric pictograms** made of round-capped bars and a disc head; and **bold bilingual type** that slides up out of masks. Every cut lands on a drum hit.
> References (grammar only): Otl Aicher's 1972 Munich pictograms (geometric athletes); multi-sport-games "look of the games" identity systems (a modular pattern + a colour set used for everything); Swiss sports-broadcast graphics (mono meta text, tick-bar progress). Learn the grammar; never copy any real event's pictograms, emblem, slogan, pattern artwork or colour names, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: ASCII / CRT 终端
styles.desc: 月球基地的 AI 沉睡 40 年后被唤醒，用字符画出“家”来回复。
styles.fit: 讲代码、讲 AI，和样片库 E3 字符画一起看
styles.prompt:
# ASCII / CRT Terminal: Style Prompt

> Everything on screen is a real character on a monospace grid, lit by the phosphor of an old monochrome CRT.
> References (grammar only): 1970s–80s monochrome terminals and teletype logs (typed output, cursor, status lines); ASCII art and demoscene text-mode pictures (images from glyph density); analog-synth film scores of the early 1980s (cold pulse, patient drones). Copy no film's interface text, fonts or logos, and use no real agency names.

styles.name: 数据叙事
styles.desc: 一百年的夏季气温，图表本身就是故事。
styles.prompt:
# Data Storytelling — Style Prompt

> A chart that tells a story: real data, drawn mark by mark on cream paper by a red–blue pencil, with handwritten notes pinned to the numbers. The chart itself is the camera, the rhythm and the plot.
> References (grammar only): Hans Rosling's *200 Countries, 200 Years, 4 Minutes* (one dot is a character), Ed Hawkins' warming stripes (a diverging ramp on a reference mean, no axes), The Pudding / NYT scrollytelling (one idea at a time, growing axes, pinned notes). Copy none of their charts, layouts or typefaces; never name them in the film.

styles.name: 等距信息图
styles.desc: 一杯咖啡从种植园到你手里的旅程。
styles.prompt:
# Isometric Infographic — Style Prompt

> A system diagram comes alive: an isometric diorama of flat three-tone blocks, thin ink labels and Isotype numbers, where things open up to show their insides and the numbers are drawn, not stated.
> References (grammar only): *Monument Valley* (true-isometric architecture, flat colour blocks, three fixed tones per face, a camera that pans and zooms but never breaks the projection); *SimCity 2000*-style cutaway dioramas (a floating board with soil strata, the whole system visible at once); Kurzgesagt (a question, a steady push forward, one clear visual metaphor per step, a change of scale when a number is too big to feel); Isotype, Otto Neurath / Gerd Arntz (repeated identical icons stand for quantity); *Powers of Ten* (a continuous dive through nested scales). Use none of their characters, buildings, icons, palettes or music.

styles.name: 暗色科技发布
styles.desc: 虚构 app Tidy 的发布片：被埋掉的光标一键把几百个窗口归位。
styles.prompt:
# Dark Tech Keynote — Style Prompt

> A software launch film where the interface itself is the star: near-black gradient, hairline grid, soft light, one brand accent, and UI that moves with snap-grid precision. Light reveals, one giant number, and a sound design that is as ordered as the pixels.
> **References (grammar only):** Apple product reveals (black stage, light sweeps, one line per screen, the lone giant number); Linear / Stripe / Vercel launch videos (snap-grid motion, 1 px lines, one accent); Steve Reich's process music (phasing, subtraction); Edgar Wright's insert cuts. Never use their names, interfaces, fonts, system controls, melodies or logos, and never name them in the film.

styles.name: 活体实机录屏
styles.desc: 像素小人 Clawd 搬进 Claude 应用，一镜到底演示 Plan 模式和自检。
styles.fit: 录屏加一个动画角色，演示"我"怎么用 AI 工具
styles.prompt:
# Living Screencast — Style Prompt

> A product walkthrough that looks like a real screen recording, where a low-resolution mascot lives inside a high-resolution interface and acts out what the software is doing.
> References (grammar only):
> - **Screen Studio-style product recordings:** auto-zoom to the cursor, cursor smoothing, click push-ins, and a window floating on wallpaper.
> - **Apple "Guided Tour" videos:** real interface, calm narration, one feature per sentence.
> - **Duolingo and Headspace mascot motion:** squash and stretch, anticipation, a character that performs inside the UI.
> - **The Browser Company (Arc) launch films:** playful tone and fast cutting.
>
> Never copy their characters, UI, music or footage.

A walkthrough of a piece of software, typically 45–75 s. The user gives the product and the features; you decide the story, shots, choreography, sound and music.

styles.name: 科幻全息界面
styles.desc: 电助力车被扫描成全息线框，目标框依次锁定电池、电机、刹车。
styles.prompt:
# Sci-fi Hologram HUD — Style Prompt

> An object is scanned into a glowing wireframe. Target boxes lock onto its parts; each opens in a local exploded view, a leader pulls out, and its number rolls from garbage glyphs into the real value. It may light up, once, into a solid hologram.
> References (grammar only): the *Iron Man* / *Avengers* HUDs (target boxes, callouts, rolling numbers, layered depth); the *Oblivion* interfaces (one colour, hairlines, space); CAD exploded views. Copy none of their layouts, icons, fonts or colours.

A **scene style**: it does a practical job (a spec walkthrough, a teardown, a loop screen) for any object with parts. See §11 for the jobs.

styles.name: 1930s 橡皮管卡通
styles.desc: 一只咖啡杯满厨房追一块逃跑的方糖。
styles.prompt:
# 1930s Rubber Hose Cartoon — Style Prompt

> Black-and-white hand-inked cartoons where every object is alive and swings to a hot jazz band.
> References (grammar only): early Fleischer Studios shorts (c. 1930–33) for "the whole world dances", surreal transformation, the bouncing-ball singalong and ink-and-pen framing devices; *Cuphead* for how a modern team finishes the look and scores it with a big band. Never use an existing cartoon character, name or silhouette, and never copy designs, melodies or logos. **Avoid the "cup-head on a human body with a straw" design**: if your hero is an object, the *whole object is the body*.

styles.name: 80 年代赛璐璐动画
styles.desc: 快递少女骑车穿过雨后霓虹都市，赶在黎明发射前送到一盘磁带。
styles.prompt:
# 80s Cel Anime — Style Prompt

> Hand-painted cel animation from the golden age of Japanese OVAs, re-created in code: flat two-tone cels over airbrushed backgrounds, backlit neon, limited-animation timing, played back as a late-80s videotape on a CRT television.
> References (grammar only): 1980s Japanese OVA and TV cel animation in general (painted-background vs flat-cel contrast, backlit light, held drawings, speed grammar, city-pop openings). Borrow the era's craft, never a specific work's characters, mecha, logos, place names or signature shots.

styles.name: 科幻情景喜剧卡通
styles.desc: 厌世天才开传送门只想买杯咖啡，却穿过越来越离谱的平行宇宙。
styles.prompt:
# Sci-Fi Sitcom Toon — Style Prompt

> Adult-animation sci-fi sitcom: thick boiling outlines, flat colour, a duo whose reactions don't match, a glowing portal, and one palette per world.
> References (grammar only): adult-swim-era sci-fi sitcom cartoons (dialogue-driven comedy, reaction close-ups, boiling line, sci-fi hardware as household junk). Borrow the *grammar*, never the characters.

styles.name: 50s 扁平卡通
styles.desc: 用 50 年代教育片的口吻，三步教你装好一台扫地机。
styles.fit: 老科普片的感觉，感知科普很合适
styles.prompt:
# Mid-century Cartoon — Style Prompt

> 1950s flat colour and limited animation for "follow along" films: colour printed a few pixels off its broken ink line, bodies that hold still while hands do the work, abstract colour-block rooms, a calm classroom narrator, and a cool-jazz combo.
> References (grammar only): UPA's early-1950s shorts (*Gerald McBoing-Boing*, *Rooty Toot Toot*): colour and line on separate cels, geometric people, colour-plane backgrounds, limited animation. 1950s classroom films (Coronet, Encyclopaedia Britannica): direct address, one sentence per picture, numbered cards. Charley Harper and Mary Blair: soft atomic-age complements, geometric figures. 1950s appliance manuals: numbered medallions, curved arrows, round call-outs, sunbursts. Copy none of their characters, drawings, lettering or music, and never name them in a film.

A **scene style**: it performs a real use (a set-up guide, a how-to, a recipe card, a safety card) rather than telling a story. The viewer should come away able to do the thing. See §11 for the jobs.

styles.name: 16-bit 像素 RPG
styles.desc: 勇士在最终 Boss 门前存档，存档画面闪回一路冒险。
styles.prompt:
# 16-bit Pixel RPG — Style Prompt

> A short film that looks, sounds and *behaves* like a mid-90s console role-playing game: 320×180 pixels, a limited indexed palette, text boxes that type, menus, save files, chip music with echo.
> References (grammar only): mid-90s console RPGs as a system of dialog boxes, menus, battles, overworlds and save points; the palette tricks of indexed hardware (palette swaps, fades by steps, cycling); the colour-depth history of consoles (4 shades → 8-bit → 16-bit). Never use existing game names, characters, UI frames, fonts, logos, melodies or sound effects. Learn the grammar, not the assets.

styles.name: HD-2D
styles.desc: 灯塔熄灭，孙女提着最后一簇火穿过夜林、爬上风暴悬崖。
styles.prompt:
# HD-2D — Style Prompt

> Hand-made pixel sprites standing like paper cut-outs inside a lit, fogged, fully 3D diorama, shot from a high three-quarter angle through a tilt-shift lens: a toy world where every lamp throws a real shadow.
> References (grammar only): *Octopath Traveler* (Square Enix × Acquire, 2018) and its sequel (2023), the games that defined the HD-2D look. Learn the grammar: sprite-in-diorama, high 3/4 camera, tilt-shift focus band, point lights with shadows, heavy bloom and vignette, framed dialogue box. Never use their characters, places, logos, UI ornaments or music, and never name them in the film.
> Name: "HD-2D" is Square Enix's term (and trademark) for that look. The library borrows it only to describe the style; this style and its demo have no connection to Square Enix and are not endorsed by it. Don't use "HD-2D" as a title or brand in a film.

styles.name: 微游戏快闪
styles.desc: 见习宇航员闯五秒训练营，越来越快，Boss 关亲手降落回地球。
styles.prompt:
# Microgame Frenzy — Style Prompt

> A rapid-fire party-game film: one command word, a few seconds, one action. Every microgame is drawn in a completely different art style, and the film keeps getting faster.
> Genre reference (grammar only): the WarioWare series. Never use its name, characters, UI, microgames or music.

The format suits short films; once the frenzy stops building, end it.

styles.name: 综艺节奏扁平
styles.desc: 把 AI 发展史做成一局节奏游戏，模型踩着拍登场，最后发成绩单。
styles.prompt:
# Game Show Flat — Style Prompt

> A rhythm-game variety show in flat vector: toy-like mascots with thick ink outlines on candy-coloured stripes and sunbursts, every hit landing on a fixed tempo grid, call-and-response patterns, and a judgement word when each round is won.
> References (grammar only): rhythm-action party games in the Rhythm Heaven mould (cue → answer, round cards, judgement words), Japanese variety-show telops (thick outlined captions, stripe and sunburst sets), WarioWare-style stage cards. Never use their names, characters, UI, levels or music.

The length follows the number of rounds: each round is a title card plus its bars of play. Narration is optional: the style can carry a film on short shouts and telops alone.

styles.prompt:
# 1920s Silent Film — Style Prompt

> An engraved-illustration silent film projected in a picture house: ink line and silver wash, a 4:3 print that flickers and weaves between velvet curtains, intertitles instead of voices, and a cinema pianist who plays every beat.
> References (grammar only): **Buster Keaton**, *The General* (1926) and *Sherlock Jr.* (1924) — the whole gag in one locked-off wide shot, a deadpan face, a body that does the acting; **Harold Lloyd**, *Safety Last!* (1923) — the near-miss; **Georges Méliès** — the iris and the trick shot; **The Artist** (2011) — how few intertitles a modern audience needs; **1920s photoplay piano cue sheets** — music by mood section, the piano doing the sound effects. Never use the Tramp look (bowler, toothbrush moustache, cane), any real film's gags, or any published melody.

# Liminal Found Footage — Style Prompt

> Camcorder tapes recovered from empty, endless, fluorescent-lit spaces. Rules instead of monsters.
> Genre reference (grammar only): "the Backrooms" internet folklore and new-weird / rule-horror; 1990s consumer camcorder footage. **Never** use the word "Backrooms", wiki "Level" numbers, community entity names, or any existing organisation or logo inside the film. Everything on screen (rules, forms, company voice, any presence) is original.

Suits short films; the length follows the walk, and the dread thins out once nothing new goes wrong.

# Style: comic book issue (cover, page turns, splash pages)

A video that stages its content as a physical vintage comic book being read on camera: a portrait-oriented comic page/spread sits centered in the landscape frame against a near-black vignette background, and a virtual camera pans and pushes into individual panels the way a motion-comic or Ken Burns documentary reveals a print page. The book opens with a magazine-style cover, then turns through several two-page spreads of a 2x2 panel grid, and closes on a colophon-style back cover. Panels are built from flat pop-art color blocks (red, gold/orange, blue), Ben-Day halftone dot textures, and sunburst ray backgrounds, with comic sound-effect bursts and a speech-bubble mascot giving it an energetic, Silver-Age-superhero-comic / 1960s advertising-comic feel. The mood is upbeat, punchy, and declarative, reinforced by a continuously driving instrumental music bed with frequent hard transient hits.

styles.name: 纪录片
styles.prompt:
# Style: documentary case file

A piece that reads like a serious investigative-documentary case file rather than a marketing reel: a near-black canvas holding a slowly turning low-poly "network sphere" emblem, chaptered like folder tabs ("Chapter 1 — ...", "Chapter 2 — ..."), with aged paper "evidence cards" laid under a desk lamp, minimal data-journalism bar charts, and one dramatized "witness testimony" segment shot as a backlit, explicitly-labeled graphic silhouette. Everything moves slowly and settles rather than snaps; captions build up phrase by phrase like narration being typed out; a hushed, low ambient bed with a slow recurring pluck tone underscores the whole thing, broken only by a hard opening hit and a bright closing chime. The net effect is hushed, credible, forensic — closer to a true-crime/60-Minutes case-file open than a tech-hype trailer.

The overall feeling is hushed, reverent, and slightly theatrical — closer to an after-hours exhibit tour than a tech product demo, with warm sepia light carving objects out of near-total black.

styles.name: 突发新闻
styles.prompt:
# Style: breaking-news broadcast

This clip resembles a cable-news "breaking news" graphics package — the kind of template a 24-hour news channel uses to announce a major story. It opens on a slowly-revealed rotating-globe title card, sweeps a diagonal tri-color ribbon across the screen for the headline stinger, cuts to a flat-vector illustrated news anchor at a desk with a persistent lower-third and scrolling ticker, pushes into a zooming world map (globe → country → city → geolocation pin), then alternates between data/stat cards and the anchor before closing on a minimal logo card. The feeling is urgent, corporate-broadcast, and info-dense: deep navy blues, hard red accents, bold condensed numerals, and a constant on-screen HUD (live clock, channel bug, ticker) that never disappears, evoking authority and immediacy rather than warmth.

styles.name: 侦探线索板
styles.fit: 把线索连起来，科普推理
styles.prompt:
# Style: detective evidence board

This clip reads like a detective's evidence corkboard being filmed and slowly revealed: a warm, lamp-lit cork bulletin board covered in pinned index cards and handwritten sticky notes, centered on a "mugshot" placeholder card for an unidentified suspect. Instead of cutting between shots, a single camera pans and tracks sideways across the board as new evidence cards appear one by one, each strung to the suspect card with taut red thread, building toward a wide "conspiracy board" pull-back. A camera-flash whiteout is the only hard cut in the video, swapping the mystery card for a clean "identified" result card stamped closed. The pacing feels like a true-crime documentary graphics package: steady ticking/pulsing music under a slow reveal, a stab of sharp hits, one big swell exactly on the flash-cut, then a fade to quiet.

The mood is warm, nostalgic, and gentle: soft pastel scene-paintings inside a locket-shaped frame, muted earth-tone data callouts, and a plush round mascot that waves through every scene. It reads as a bedtime-story explainer: cozy rather than corporate, tactile rather than flat-UI.

A thin scanline texture sits over every frame, and a chiptune-style pulsing melody drives the pacing. The overall feeling is nostalgic, toy-like, and gamified — factual/data content (benchmark scores, price changes) is translated one-to-one into RPG game-feel (quest completion bars, "+EXP" pickups, loot cards, stat increases).

# Style: TV weather forecast

A short data video styled as a Korean TV nightly-weather-report broadcast graphics package repurposed for a status update. It opens with a satellite/radar-style storm-spiral animation, then cuts through a sequence of "forecast card" scenes — a temperature-style map, thermometers, wind/speed gauges, a multi-day forecast strip, and a sunny sign-off — each dressed with real broadcast chrome: a channel logo pill, a live date badge, and a scrolling breaking-news ticker along the bottom. The screen stays locked-off and flat; all motion lives inside the graphics (falling snow, twinkling stars, drifting wind lines, a fast diagonal wipe between scenes). A bright, plucky instrumental loop runs under it with an accented musical hit landing on every scene change, giving the whole thing a polished, on-air, slightly playful newsroom feel.

styles.prompt:
# Style: home-shopping infomercial

The video reads as a parody of a Korean late-night TV home-shopping / infomercial broadcast: a flat, rounded-vector cartoon world where each beat of the pitch gets its own full-bleed, single-hue "sunburst" backdrop, a chunky comic-shout headline slams onto the screen, and a persistent lower-third news-ticker bar keeps scrolling bullet claims underneath. A simple blob-shaped mascot character stands in for "the customer," shown gloomy and gray before the pitch and pumped-up and colorful after it. There is no camera movement at all — it behaves like a slide deck of hard graphic cards, each card populated with big bold numbers, price tags, comparison panels, and cartoon icons (a ticking bomb, a ringing phone, a rocket, a green checkmark). The audio is a bright, dense, evenly-pulsing music-and-SFX bed that stays "hot" almost the entire runtime, occasionally spiking with comedic riser/whoosh effects timed to the hard cuts, giving the whole thing a caffeinated, game-show-auction energy.

styles.name: 体育直播
styles.prompt:
# Style: sports broadcast

The clip reads like a cable-TV live-sports broadcast package — a night-match stadium open with floodlights and an LED-dot crowd, cut with the on-screen graphics package a network overlays during a match (score bug, "LIVE" badge, lower-third source ticker) — repurposed to walk through a head-to-head stat comparison instead of a game. Motion is entirely 2D broadcast-graphics motion (nothing pans or dollies; text counts up, bars fill, cards slide and glow) cut into short hard-cut chapters every few seconds. The audio is a rhythmic, plucked/percussive pulse that tightens and loosens with the on-screen drama — quieter during the analytical stat-sheet beat, swelling into a bright, confetti-timed climax at the finale — which together with the broadcast chrome gives it the feel of a TV "match highlights" reel rather than a slide deck.

styles.name: 组装说明书
styles.fit: 讲步骤，宜家说明书那种
styles.prompt:
# Style: assembly manual

The video reads like a printed IKEA-style product-assembly instruction booklet that has been turned into a motion explainer: flat vector line art on aged cream paper, a giant chapter numeral opening every page, an isometric shipping-box "hero" object, a small stick-figure mascot for scale, and literal hardware metaphors (price tags, coin stacks, a conveyor belt, wall outlets) standing in for abstract data instead of ordinary charts. Pages slide over one another like leaves of a manual being turned rather than cutting, each diagram builds itself piece by piece before its number snaps in, and a steady rhythmic tick-track under occasional synth swells gives the whole thing a calm, deliberate, "assembled and verified" feeling that ends on a stamped checkmark held in a still frame.

styles.name: 白板讲课
styles.prompt:
# Style: whiteboard lecture

A static "desk-cam" shot of a physical whiteboard, framed by its own aluminum bezel, on which a hand entering from the bottom-right corner writes, draws, underlines, circles, and erases with dry-erase markers and a block eraser — the classic hand-drawn whiteboard-explainer look. Everything is built stroke-by-stroke in real time rather than fading in, numbers get crossed out and replaced live, and nothing is ever fully wiped clean: every earlier section keeps ghosting through as a barely-visible watermark under the current one, giving the board a used, palimpsest-like texture. The mood is brisk, corporate-friendly, and a little playful (circled step numbers, a green checkmark shield, a red circled callout), riding a continuous, steady percussive beat underneath.

styles.name: 电影预告片
styles.fit: 下期预告、频道预告，11 段可以试
styles.prompt:
# Style: movie trailer

A prestige announcement trailer that reads like a luxury-watch or car-launch teaser borrowed for a tech reveal: an ultra-wide cinematic letterbox holds a near-black, warm vignette sky sprinkled with slow-drifting dust motes, and every idea — a question, then a date, then a run of benchmark numbers, then the product name, then a release date — gets its own held, centered, fully-faded screen. Nothing cuts hard; everything breathes in as a soft bloom of light, holds, and dissolves through black into the next. The mood is confident and expensive rather than energetic: hushed opening, a rhythmic pulse of swelling hits under the numbers, one big flare-and-impact at the name reveal, then a slow decrescendo fade-out.

styles.name: 数学证明讲课
styles.prompt:
# Style: math proof lecture

A dark, quiet, textbook-like explainer that stages an argument the way a math lecture stages a proof: a title card, a numbered "lemma" per claim, and a closing "therefore" statement with a QED mark. Everything sits on a near-black panel with a faint off-center glow, rendered as flat 2D vector graphics — thin-stroke bar and scatter charts, color-coded equations that build term by term, and small dim citation text in the corner. The mood is restrained and confident rather than flashy: no camera movement, no particle effects, just clean typography and numbers arriving in a steady, metronomic rhythm under a soft ambient pulse.

styles.desc: 一点透视的雨夜窄街，两边挂满竖招牌，青色的雾越远越浓，街尽头一团暖光；湿地面上的倒影占了半个画面。

styles.prompt: 黄昏的大渐变天，三层平涂的城市剪影，屋顶上一块"夜城"大霓虹字，一个人和一只猫坐在楼边，后面一列轻轨开过。

styles.name: 翼
styles.desc: 用 three.js 搭的一战空战，按 1927 年正色片拷贝调色：天空发白、黑位很深、整体琥珀染色、片门抖动和划痕。《翼》最出名的是把摄影机绑在飞机上拍的空战，所以这里大部分机位都装在飞机上。
styles.fit: 默片 3D 空战 · 正色片黑白 + 琥珀染色
styles.prompt:
平滑着色的 3D 按默片正色片拷贝调色：高反差，红色发黑。天空近白，地面留清楚的中灰层次，深黑占画面 25%–35%，只在剪影里。染色：白位向琥珀 #FFCC80 混一半，天空是淡奶油琥珀，不要整片橙；黑位不变。只有故事围绕的那个主角留色，整个人都留，饱和度约七成（如 #D97757）；灯火和其他光源一律是灰的。叠 24 fps 片门抖动（±1 像素）、闪烁（±5%）、细颗粒（±4%）、一到三条细划痕、稀疏灰尘，片门圆角加柔和暗角，第一镜 1 秒圆形光圈打开。招牌镜头：机位绑在跟主角一起动的东西上，露出一截支架，轻微震动；再接跟拍和主观镜头。每 2–3 秒一切，穿过云、烟或强光白场转场。对标 William Wellman《翼》（1927）。避免：运动模糊、灰阶里有颜色。

---

English:

Smooth-shaded 3D graded as a silent-era orthochromatic print: high contrast, reds go black. Sky near-white, ground in readable mid-greys, deep blacks (25-35% of frame) only in silhouettes. Tint: blend whites half-way toward amber #FFCC80, so the sky is pale cream-amber, never solid orange; blacks stay black. Only the hero the story centres on keeps colour, whole figure at ~70% saturation (e.g. #D97757); every lamp, fire or other light source stays grey. 24 fps gate weave (±1 px), flicker (±5%), fine grain (±4%), 1-3 thin scratches, sparse dust, rounded corners, vignette; open on a 1 s iris. Signature shot: a camera rigged to something moving with the subject, rig in frame; then chase and POV. Cut every 2-3 s; white out through cloud, smoke or glare. Reference: William Wellman, *Wings* (1927). Avoid: motion blur, colour in the greys.

styles.name: 百老汇旋律
styles.desc: 会动的黑金银装饰艺术歌舞海报：喷枪渐变、阶梯形台口、镀铬电容麦克风。1929 年的百老汇正是装饰艺术盛期，这部又是有声片降临的一部，所以让声波从麦克风里一圈圈放出来。
styles.fit: 黑金银装饰艺术歌舞海报
styles.prompt:
装饰艺术歌舞海报。黑漆底；金和银都用分带金属渐变做（每个面 3–5 条硬分界），喷枪光晕、放射线、阶梯形、流线型，场景外圈套一道层层退进的金线台口框，嵌一排灯泡。色板按用途：底 #0A0908，金 #D6B560，高光 #F3E2A2，银 #BFC4C9；皮肤用淡银奶油色；只有故事围绕的那个主角用一个饱和强调色（如 #D97757）。人物是 Erté 式修长造型，有五官表情，题材允许时加流苏、亮片或羽毛。细颗粒、闪光点、星星。正面对称，中间一束追光。动起来：灯泡流动，一排重复元素（舞者、浪头）向中心卷成波浪，主要声源或光源放射环纹；镜头慢推，踩音乐的拍子切，无乐每 2–3 秒一切。对标 A. M. Cassandre 的海报、Erté 的服装设计。避免：平涂黄色冒充金属、人物没脸、多余的颜色。

---

English:

Art Deco revue poster. Black lacquer ground; gold and silver from banded metallic gradients (3-5 hard bands); airbrush glows, sunbursts, ziggurat steps, streamlined curves; a stepped proscenium frame of gold lines and bulbs. Palette: ground #0A0908, gold #D6B560, highlight #F3E2A2, silver #BFC4C9; skin pale silver-cream; one saturated accent (e.g. #D97757) only on the hero the story centres on. Elongated Erté-style figures with real faces; fringe, sequins or feathers where the subject allows. Fine grain, glints, stars. Frontal symmetry, a central spotlight. Motion: chasing bulbs, a row of repeated elements (dancers, waves, columns) rippling toward the centre, rings radiating from the main sound or light source; slow pushes, cut on the music's beat (without music, every 2-3 s). References: A. M. Cassandre's posters, Erté's costumes. Avoid: flat yellow for metal, faceless figures, extra hues.

styles.name: 西线无战事
styles.en: All Quiet on the Western Front
styles.desc: 珂勒惠支式木刻：大块的黑、刀刻的白轮廓、粗糙木纹，Clawd 用单独一块橙色版套印。珂勒惠支 1921–22 年的反战版画，和这部片出自同一场战争、同一种悲痛。
styles.prompt:
仿凯绥·珂勒惠支《战争》组画（1921–22）的表现主义木刻。画面六到七成是实黑；形体之间用白色轮廓刀分开，刀宽为画幅宽的 1/300–1/150；人脸刻成白形，只留几笔黑五官；手要大。人物占满画面，被画框裁切。每刀都有尖的进刀收刀和碎木边，离光越近的刀越宽，刀痕成组排、节奏略不均。墨色 #17130F 印在 #E8DFCA 纸上；纹理只有木纹条和缺墨斑点（±5%）。只有故事围绕的那个主角套一块色版（如 #D97757），平铺在身体或衣服上，刀痕照样压在上面，黑仍占六成以上。光只从一个开口进来（窗、云缝）；灯只刻一小圈短刀痕。人物脚下的地面留不刻的黑。动作安静（呼吸、一个小手势）；慢摇、慢推。避免：灰雾灰调、排刀规整成条纹、血腥。

---

English:

Expressionist woodcut after Käthe Kollwitz, *Krieg* (1921-22). 60-70% solid black; white contour cuts 1/300-1/150 of frame width separate forms; faces are white shapes with a few black features; hands large. Figures fill the frame, cropped by its edges. Each cut tapers in and out with chipped edges, is wider the nearer it sits to the light, in slightly uneven bundles. Ink #17130F on paper #E8DFCA; texture is only wood-grain streaks and under-inked speckle (±5%). One colour block (e.g. #D97757) only on the hero the story centres on, flat on its body or clothes, cuts over it; black stays 60%+. Light enters through one opening (window, cloud gap); lamps get a short ring of cuts. The ground under figures stays uncut black. Quiet motion (breathing, a small gesture); slow pans and push-ins. Avoid: grey fog or midtones, even striped hatching, gore.

styles.name: 壮志千秋
styles.desc: 1889 年的金调色蛋白印相全景：柔焦、轻微的横向拖影、奶油高光和暖褐暗部、银盐颗粒，只有 Clawd 手工上色。片子开场就是 1889 年俄克拉何马圈地狂奔，用那一年的照片质感来拍，这一章也保持单色。
styles.prompt:
会动的 1880 年代金调色蛋白照片。先画边缘柔和的平涂形，按亮度分：主体深（15%–30%），地面 50%–60%，天空约 90%；物面和草丛有看得见的排线（线宽约画幅宽 1/300）。再“印”：转灰度，轻柔焦（约画幅宽 1/800），三层横向错开的淡影随运镜拉长，乘奶油色 #F2DCB4，黑位抬成暖褐 #2E1C0F，显影不匀（±5%），暗角压到 #785634，每帧刷新颗粒（±4%），稀疏灰尘划痕。只给故事围绕的那个主角手工上色（如 #D97757），像透明染料，蒙版羽化 2–3 像素；灯光仍是棕褐。横向全景，中间一条带排满重复小元素：人物、动物、车辆，题材冷清就用篱笆、木桩、树；别让一整块大面占满画面。天空默认发白。运镜：从主角近景 4–5 秒缓出拉到全景。避免：硬墨线、主角以外的颜色、干净的数码天空、发灰的印相。

---

English:

A moving 1880s gold-toned albumen photograph. Paint soft-edged flat shapes by brightness: main subjects dark (15-30%), ground 50-60%, sky about 90%; visible hatching and grass tufts (lines ~1/300 of frame width). Then print: grayscale, slight blur (~1/800 of frame width), a faint smear of three horizontal offset copies growing with camera speed, multiply cream #F2DCB4, lift blacks to umber #2E1C0F, blotchy development (±5%), vignette to #785634, per-frame grain (±4%), dust, scratches. Hand-tint only the hero the story centres on (e.g. #D97757) as transparent dye, mask feathered 2-3 px; lamps stay sepia. Wide panorama: the middle band packed with repeated small elements (figures, animals, vehicles; for a lone subject fences, posts, trees), no big plane dominating. Camera: one 4-5 s ease-out pull back from the hero to the panorama. Avoid: hard ink outlines, colour beyond the hero, a flat grey print.

styles.name: 大饭店
styles.desc: 用 three.js 建的圆形大堂，按米高梅的银色黑白调色，Clawd 的橙是唯一的颜色。这部片最出名的是从顶上笔直往下拍、回廊一圈圈收进去的镜头，整个布景就按这一镜来建。
styles.fit: 米高梅银色黑白 3D 大堂
styles.prompt:
真 3D 场景，默认装饰艺术风大堂（大理石、镀铬、吊灯、亮面棋盘格地面）；室外保留真实场景，表面做出光泽（湿路面、静水），构图对称。环境光遮蔽加柔和辉光，调成 30 年代片厂银色黑白：约四成画面深黑，白位亮度约九成，不发灰。光从一个高处光源成束落下。只有故事围绕的那个主角留色（如 #D97757），至少占画面高度六分之一；暖灯渲染成白光，辉光只在灯旁。颗粒（±3%），灯旁光晕。招牌镜头：平视大全景，望进对称纵深，地面和天花同时入画，地面有倒影；再接 4–6 秒的侧向跟拍；俯拍同心圆、人像棋子只用一次。年代人物有头、帽、四肢，按路线走。对标美术指导 Cedric Gibbons、摄影师 William Daniels。避免：原地踏步、抽象图案铺满画面、偏色。

---

English:

A real 3D set, by default an Art Deco interior (marble, chrome, chandelier, glossy checkerboard floor); outdoors keep the real setting with glossy surfaces (wet pavement, still water) and symmetrical framing. Ambient occlusion, soft bloom; 1930s studio silver: about 40% deep black, glossy whites near 90%, no washed-out greys. Light falls in shafts from one high source. All neutral grey except the hero the story centres on (e.g. #D97757), at least 1/6 of frame height; warm lamps render white, bloom only around them. Grain (±3%), halation. Signature shot: eye-height wide into a deep symmetrical set, floor and ceiling in frame, floor reflections; then 4-6 s tracks; one overhead on rings, figures as chess pieces. Period figures (heads, hats, limbs) walk routes. References: art director Cedric Gibbons, cinematographer William Daniels. Avoid: walking in place, frame-filling abstract patterns, colour casts.

styles.name: 乱世春秋
styles.desc: 慕夏式新艺术装饰画：膨胀的褐色轮廓线、粉彩平涂、马赛克底，中心人物身后一个光环。电影开场就是 1899 年跨年夜一家人举杯迎接新世纪，所以光环做成敲十二点的钟面。
styles.prompt:
慕夏式彩色石印。褐色 #4B3326 轮廓线，宽约画幅宽 1/250，背光侧（光默认从左上来）加粗到两倍，两端收尖；粉彩平涂，每块在背光侧叠一层深一档的硬边色。色板：奶油 #F5ECD6 作纸和天空，鼠尾草绿 #A9B490 作植物衣褶，淡金 #CFA55A 作光环装饰，玫瑰 #DBA49C 作皮肤和花；故事围绕的那个主角用一个更浓的强调色（如 #D97757）。横幅：人物和细环纹大光环居中三分之一，两侧拱格，后面铺灰青（鼠尾草绿掺灰）方块马赛克；鞭线藤蔓和花草；底部一条衬线大写铭文，用用户语言，字高约画面 1/25。留白不超过画面八分之一。杏仁眼、厚眼睑；头发或衣料三色成束。石版颗粒、纸斑、暗角。慢摆；下摇到光环再拉远。避免：干净细线、饱和色、空荡背景。

---

English:

Alphonse Mucha colour lithograph. Brown contours #4B3326, about 1/250 of frame width, doubling on the shadow side (light from upper left), tapered ends; pastel flats, each with a hard-edged darker shadow tone. Palette: cream #F5ECD6 paper/sky, sage #A9B490 foliage/drapery, pale gold #CFA55A halo/ornament, rose #DBA49C skin/flowers; the hero the story centres on in one stronger accent (e.g. #D97757). Wide frame: figure and a big ring-filled halo in the middle third, arched panels either side, behind them a muted-teal (sage plus grey) square-tile mosaic; whiplash vines, local flowers; a bottom band of serif capitals in the user's language, 1/25 of frame height. No plain area over 1/8 of frame. Almond eyes, heavy lids; hair or cloth in three-tone strands. Litho grain, paper mottle, vignette. Slow sway; tilt down to the halo, pull back. Avoid: thin clean lines, saturated colour, empty backgrounds.

styles.name: 一夜风流
styles.desc: 1934 年的黑白橡皮管卡通：粗细变化的墨线、饼切眼、白手套，赛璐璐平涂叠在灰阶水彩背景上，带胶片颗粒。和电影同一年，公路喜剧的笑点也适合卡通的节奏。
styles.prompt:
30 年代初的黑白橡皮管卡通。角色：软管四肢、白手套、饼切眼、圆脑袋，三到四头身；墨线 #141414 粗细变化（画幅宽 1/400–1/150），背光一侧变粗（默认光从左上）；角色平涂只用纯黑、纯白，加至多一种浅灰作硬阴影，黑面一道高光。背景只用中间灰（明度 30%–80%），不用纯黑白：铅笔线不擦，灰色水彩罩染，边缘积水有颗粒沉淀。只有故事围绕的那个主角带颜色（如 #D97757）：整个身体，主角是人时只给关键道具。加 ±1 像素片门抖动、24 fps 颗粒（±4%）、闪烁、划痕、灰尘。动作都有预备、冲过头再回落：落地压扁、快动拉长、吃惊时弹眼，碰撞时镜头轻震。对标弗莱舍工作室的 Betty Boop 短片、迪士尼《糊涂交响曲》的背景。避免：光滑矢量线、角色发灰和背景糊在一起。

---

English:

Early-1930s black-and-white rubber-hose cartoon. Characters: noodle limbs, white gloves, pie-cut eyes, round heads; thick-thin ink #141414 (1/400-1/150 of frame width) swelling away from the light (default upper left); fills pure black and white plus at most one light grey for the hard shadow, gloss on blacks. Backgrounds stay mid-grey (30-80%), never pure black/white: graphite lines left in, grey watercolour washes with pooled edges and granulation, paper grain. Only the hero the story centres on has colour (e.g. #D97757): its whole body, or its one key prop if the hero is human. ±1 px gate weave, grain (±4%), flicker, scratches, dust. Actions anticipate, overshoot, settle: squash on landing, stretch on fast moves, eyes pop when surprised, a camera jolt on hits. References: Fleischer's Betty Boop shorts; Disney's Silly Symphonies backgrounds. Avoid: smooth vector lines, grey characters merging with the background.

styles.name: 叛舰喋血记
styles.desc: 18 世纪英国海军部海图的铜版画：恒向线、罗盘玫瑰、水深数字、手工淡彩，邦蒂号是图上的一幅船舶插画。这部片讲的是一次航行，所以整段都留在海图上。
styles.prompt:
18 世纪末的铜版地图，默认是英国海军部海图（内陆题材换成测绘图）。明暗全靠刻刀细排线和交叉排线，线宽约画幅宽的 1/1200；线宽设下限，细小处变暗而不是消失。墨色 #1C1610 印在 #EFE3C4 直纹纸上，带淡霉斑和折痕。只上很薄的手工淡彩：沿水边的海蓝 #9EBCBC，陆地 #B8C08C；故事围绕的那个主角（如 #D97757）是唯一的浓色。32 向罗盘玫瑰拉出恒向线网、刻度边框、晕滃山形、装饰图名框、一个装饰物（如海怪）、衬线字。情节放进一幅不加边框的排线插画，排线向纸面渐隐；推到底时插画占画面高度 60%–75%。运镜：一个 5–6 秒的镜头从整张图滑进插画，四周留着地图；一条虚线路线自己画出来。避免：切出纸面、浓重水彩、僵硬的人物。

---

English:

A late-18th-century copperplate map, default an Admiralty sea chart (inland: a survey map). Fine burin hatching and cross-hatching (lines ~1/1200 of frame width) give all tone; a minimum line width makes small detail darken, not vanish. Ink #1C1610 on laid paper #EFE3C4, light foxing, folds. Thin hand colour: water #9EBCBC along edges, land #B8C08C; the hero the story centres on (e.g. #D97757) is the one strong colour. Rhumb lines from 32-point roses, a graduated border, hachured hills, cartouche, one ornament (e.g. a sea monster), serif lettering. Put the action in an unboxed engraved vignette fading into the chart, filling 60-75% of frame height at the end of the move. Camera: one 5-6 s glide from the whole sheet into the vignette, chart still around it; a dotted route inks itself in. Avoid: cropping the paper, heavy washes, stiff figures.

styles.name: 歌舞大王齐格飞
styles.desc: 用 three.js 建的旋转螺旋“婚礼蛋糕”舞台，米高梅银色黑白：缎面、雪纺和鸵鸟羽毛衬在深黑里，只有 Clawd 是颜色。《A Pretty Girl Is Like a Melody》那座 175 级的螺旋舞台是这部片的名场面。
styles.fit: 银色黑白 3D 螺旋婚礼蛋糕舞台
styles.prompt:
真 3D 舞台大场面，调成 30 年代片厂银色黑白：把题材的世界搭成圆形分层转台上的歌舞布景，慢慢转（每秒约 3 度），挂满垂幔花环；题材里的人变成一排排穿戏服、有脸有手的合唱队。灰阶：戏服浅缎灰，布景中灰，褶皱大幕更深，剧场深黑；白色不到纯白。正面柔和主光，轮廓光更亮，把缎子和羽毛的边勾到近白。淡光柱，颗粒（±3%）。只有故事围绕的那个主角留色（如 #D97757），灯都渲染成白光。招牌镜头：贴低的中景沿层台看过去，人物占画面高度四分之一到三分之一，主角在前排。再接帷幕升起（3 秒）、10 秒吊臂上升，落到平视主角的中景。对标 Robert Z. Leonard《歌舞大王齐格飞》（1936）。避免：平均打光、没脸的锥形人、转得太快。

---

English:

Real 3D stage spectacle in 1930s studio silver: the subject's world built as a revue set on a round tiered platform turning about 3° per second, draped and garlanded; its people become rows of costumed chorus figures with faces and arms. Costumes light satin grey, set mid-grey, pleated curtain backdrop darker, theatre deep black; whites below pure white. Soft front key; brighter rim lights edging satin and feathers near-white. Faint shafts, grain (±3%). All neutral grey except the hero the story centres on (e.g. #D97757); lamps render white. Signature shot: low medium along the tiers, figures 1/4-1/3 of frame height, the hero on the front tier. Then a 3 s curtain rise, a 10 s crane up to a level medium of the hero. Reference: Robert Z. Leonard, *The Great Ziegfeld* (1936). Avoid: flat lighting, faceless cones, fast spinning.

styles.name: 左拉传
styles.desc: 报纸活字印刷加 1890 年代线刻插图：木活字大标题、密排铅字正文，泛黄新闻纸上的油墨外扩和缺墨，人物用排线画。这部片最有名的画面就是 1898 年 1 月 13 日《震旦报》的《我控诉》头版。
styles.fit: 报纸活字印刷 + 线刻插图
styles.prompt:
1890 年代的报纸印刷。文字先排成清晰墨版再“印”：约 1 像素模糊加噪声阈值切边，做出油墨外扩、字边毛糙、局部缺墨、淡淡的背面镜像透字。版面语法：报头、横贯全宽的木活字大标题（约画面高度 1/6）、3–6 栏小字正文（用用户的语言，字高约画面 1/80）夹着一幅大线刻插图。木活字一字一块，带木纹。所有画面都是线刻：线宽约画幅宽 1/1000、间距约 1/400，顺着形体走，交叉排线只用在暗部，背光一侧轮廓加粗，远处用淡墨。暖黑 #17130F 印在新闻纸 #E8E0CC 上；故事围绕的那个主角单独一块强调色版（如 #D97757），套印偏 1–2 像素。动起来：活字块砸下、回弹、留下印迹；一个反复的机械动作，报纸翻页。避免：干净的数码字体、平滑灰调、其他颜色。

---

English:

1890s newspaper print. Set text as a sharp mask, then print: ~1 px blur and a noisy threshold for ink spread, ragged edges, under-inked patches, faint mirrored show-through. Page grammar: masthead, a wood-type headline across the width (~1/6 of frame height), 3-6 columns of small type in the user's language (~1/80 of frame height) flanking one large engraved picture. Wood-type letters are grained blocks. Everything pictured is a line engraving: hatching lines about 1/1000 of frame width, spaced 1/400, following the form, cross-hatching only in darks, heavier shadow-side contours, paler distance. Warm black #17130F on newsprint #E8E0CC; the hero the story centres on gets one accent plate (e.g. #D97757), offset 1-2 px. Motion: type blocks slam down, bounce and leave their print; one repeating mechanical motion, pages turning. Avoid: clean digital type, smooth grey shading, other colours.

styles.name: 浮生若梦
styles.en: You Can't Take It with You
styles.desc: 30 年代 WPA 丝网海报：六色不透明平涂油墨、分色渐变、轻微套印错位，印在棉浆纸上。1936–39 年联邦艺术计划的海报就是这部片同年代的美国平面语言，也和第 10 部的报纸拉开距离。
styles.prompt:
1936–39 年 WPA 联邦艺术计划的丝网海报。六色不透明油墨从浅到深套印，后印的版要在不该盖住的浅色形（云、太阳、高光）处镂空：奶油 #F0E2C0 给光和云，赭 #E0A842、朱红 #C84A2A 给天空和暖色面，青 #22686E 给水和阴影，主角专用色（如 #D97757，只用在故事围绕的那个主角身上），最后印深棕描边 #322018。阴影是深一色叠印，不用灰。大面积用分色渐变：两色 2–3 级粗台阶，中间一级是两色叠印。每版套偏 1–3 像素，模版边缘游移，刮板拖痕、漏印，平涂上都有暖色棉浆纸纹（±5%）。人物占画面高度二分之一到三分之二：大块面、月牙形暗面、棕色描边、脸有表情。留一条粗体大写标题，用用户的语言。慢推，一版一版弹出来。避免：网点、平滑渐变、干净的矢量平涂。

---

English:

A 1936-39 WPA (Federal Art Project) silkscreen poster. Six opaque inks printed light to dark, each later screen cut away around lighter shapes (clouds, sun): cream #F0E2C0 for light, ochre #E0A842 and vermilion #C84A2A for sky and warm planes, teal #22686E for water and shade, the hero's own ink (e.g. #D97757, only on the hero the story centres on), brown keyline #322018 last. Shadows: a darker ink overprinted, never grey. Big areas get split-fountain blends: two inks in 2-3 coarse steps, the middle one their overprint. Screens 1-3 px off register; wandering stencil edges, squeegee streaks, warm rag-paper grain (±5%) on every flat. Figures fill 1/2-2/3 of frame height: big planes, crescent shadows, expressive faces. A bold capital title band, user's language. Slow pushes; screens pop in one by one. Avoid: halftone dots, smooth gradients, clean vector flats.

styles.name: 乱世佳人
styles.desc: 厚涂油画：刮刀色块、颜料堆起的棱，Technicolor 的热度——从金色烧到血红的天空、红土、黑色剪影。全片的色彩从《乱世佳人》开始降临，第一张满色画面就是夕阳下的塔拉。
styles.prompt:
1939 年 Technicolor 配色的厚涂油画。刮刀色块：天空用长条横向色带（长为画幅宽的 1/15–1/6，厚约 1/60），地面和人物用顺形体的短笔触，之间留出平静、薄涂的区域；颜料棱受左上方的光，越亮越厚，薄处露布纹。默认是落日天空，从酒红 #3A0912 经大红 #A8241A、橙 #F27A22 烧到金 #FFD878；地面红褐 #6E2214；剪影是带暖意的近黑；故事围绕的那个主角保持看得清的暖中间调（如 #D97757），不做成剪影。强逆光，金色轮廓光；近景加一道暖色侧光照亮半边脸和手。构图像史诗海报：大块深色剪影（树、房子、岩石、人物）压在低地平线上。灯火用油画火焰。运镜：全景慢推，低机位推近主角，最后吊臂升起看大景。避免：大小一样的碎块铺满画面、脏棕色、平滑渐变。

---

English:

Impasto oil in a 1939 Technicolor palette. Palette-knife slabs: long horizontal sky bands (1/15-1/6 of frame width long, about 1/60 tall), shorter strokes following form on land and figures, calm thin areas between; ridges lit from upper left, paint thickest in highlights, canvas weave where thin. Default sunset sky: wine #3A0912, red #A8241A, orange #F27A22, gold #FFD878; ground red-brown #6E2214; warm near-black silhouettes. The hero the story centres on stays a readable warm mid-tone (e.g. #D97757), never a silhouette. Strong backlight, gold rims; in close shots a warm side light on half the face and hands. Epic-poster composition: big dark silhouettes (trees, buildings, rocks, figures) on a low horizon. Lamps as painted flames. Camera: slow push on the wide, low push-in on the hero, crane up to a vista. Avoid: tiled same-size strokes, muddy browns, smooth gradients.

styles.name: 蝴蝶梦
styles.desc: 粗纹纸上的炭笔画：天鹅绒般的黑、抹开的灰，月光和雾用橡皮擦出来。希区柯克的《蝴蝶梦》是一场黑白哥特梦，庄园先在雾里、后在火里，炭笔两样都画得出来。
styles.prompt:
有纹的纸上画炭笔。纸纹细（颗粒约画幅宽 1/600）：轻压只挂纹峰，重压填满纹谷。颗粒只在中间调；黑如天鹅绒，擦白是干净纸面。明暗：约六成画面暗到中灰，一成半深黑，在最近的前景和最大块面上，亮处少。炭色 #121111，纸色 #EEECE7。笔法：藤炭干笔断线，炭条侧锋顺形体宽扫（宽为画幅宽 1/60–1/30），排线，手指抹，橡皮擦出边光和光晕；雾是在铺好的灰调上横向擦出来的（如 William Kentridge 的动画素描）。只有故事围绕的那个主角用粉彩（如 #D97757），铺得较实、透点纸纹，炭笔勾边；火焰保持炭黑和纸白。月光从上方来，两三层雾带不同速横漂。运镜：主观镜头慢推，前景向两边分开。避免：数码噪点、光滑的数码光晕、发灰的黑、空亮的天空。

---

English:

Charcoal on toothed paper. Fine tooth (grain ~1/600 of frame width): light pressure catches only the peaks, heavy pressure fills the valleys. Grain only in midtones; velvet blacks, clean-paper lifts. Values: ~60% dark-to-mid grey, 15% deep black in the nearest foreground and largest masses, lights small. Charcoal #121111 on paper #EEECE7. Marks: broken vine lines, side-of-the-stick sweeps (1/60-1/30 of frame width) following form, hatching, finger smudges, eraser lifts for edges and glows; mist is horizontal streaks erased out of a toned area (as in William Kentridge's animated drawings). Only the hero the story centres on is in pastel (e.g. #D97757), laid fairly solid, tooth peeking through, outlined in charcoal; flames stay charcoal-and-paper. Moonlight from above; 2-3 fog bands drift at different speeds. Camera: slow subjective push, foreground parting. Avoid: digital noise, smooth digital glows, grey blacks, empty bright skies.

styles.name: 青山翠谷
styles.desc: 用 1941 年原海报金黄加绿配色的不透明水粉：扎实的色块、煤黑的渣山、Kyffin Williams 式厚重的深色山体和断续描边。用水粉而不用木刻，和第 3 部区分开；画的是矿工唱着歌走下山谷回家。
styles.prompt:
仿威尔士画家 Kyffin Williams 的不透明水粉。方向性笔触宽为画幅宽 1/80–1/40，长是宽的 2–5 倍，边缘毛糙，完全覆盖；房子、墙、山脊用断续深色短线勾边；暗山上刮几笔亮绿或灰蓝。色板：天空和光淡金 #F1C565（别成芥末黄），田野绿 #86A03F，暗部煤黑 #1D1B1E，远山和水面灰蓝 #48505E，小点缀黄 #F6CF2F，其他颜色由这几色调出；故事围绕的那个主角用 #D97757，至少占画面高八分之一。田野和天空偏亮（约六成），山和房子偏暗。暖色调色不超过一成，暗角，颗粒。默认傍晚低角度侧光，田野受光，山脊有轮廓光。从高处真透视取景，一条路把视线引下去；小房子（或墙、石块）顺山坡一级级排开。动起来：烟或云循环飘动，横向跟拍。避免：水彩透明感、矢量平涂、发暗发脏。

---

English:

Opaque gouache after Welsh painter Kyffin Williams. Directional strokes 1/80-1/40 of frame width, 2-5 times as long, ragged, fully covering; broken dark dashes outline buildings, walls and ridges; dark hills flecked with lighter green or slate knife marks. Palette: sky and light pale gold #F1C565 (not mustard), fields green #86A03F, darks coal #1D1B1E, far hills and water slate #48505E, small accents yellow #F6CF2F, other colours mixed from these; the hero the story centres on #D97757, at least 1/8 of frame height. Fields and sky light (~60%), hills and buildings dark. Warm grade under 10%, vignette, grain. Default low late-afternoon side light: fields lit, ridges rim-lit. From high ground in true perspective, a path leading the eye down; small repeated buildings (or walls, rocks) stepping along slopes. Motion: looping smoke or cloud, a lateral track. Avoid: watercolour transparency, vector fills, mud.

styles.name: 忠勇之家
styles.desc: 二战英国本土战线的石印海报：砖红、深绿、奶油、灰蓝的有限套色，阴影是石版蜡笔颗粒。配影片结尾：被炸穿屋顶的乡村教堂里全村唱诗，喷火式战机从破洞上方飞过。
styles.prompt:
做成 1942 年英国战时的石印海报。造型简化有力，三版套印，略错位 1–3 像素：色版承载所有平涂；冷灰蓝蜡笔版压暗每一处阴影，带短而斜的石纹颗粒（不用网点）；墨绿黑轮廓版给每个形描一圈约画幅宽 1/500 的线，人物和云也要描。配色按用途：奶油 #EBDFC2 是纸色和亮部，灰蓝 #8497A6 是天空和阴影，砖红 #A23F2D 和深绿 #34503F 只作点缀，合计不超过画面四分之一；棕色和肤色由奶油加砖红调出；轮廓色 #1E2422。场景可以排满。天空用喷枪渐变，只有纸纹每秒 12 帧跳动。浅色光带顺着光源方向斜落，照到之处阴影版消失。人物正面站立，像海报里的人。镜头慢移带视差、上摇。对标 Frank Newbould、Abram Games。避免：网点阴影、干净的矢量边、大片饱和色。

---

English:

A 1942 British wartime stone-lithograph poster. Simple, strong shapes from three plates, 1-3 px off register: a colour plate with all flat fills; a grey-blue crayon plate darkening every shadow with short slanted stone grain; a green-black key line about 1/500 of frame width around every shape, figures and clouds included. Palette by role: cream #EBDFC2 paper and highlights, grey-blue #8497A6 sky and shadow, brick red #A23F2D and deep green #34503F as accents, at most a quarter of the frame; browns and skin mixed from cream and brick; key #1E2422. Scenes may be full. Airbrushed skies; only the paper grain boils at 12 fps. Pale light bands, angled from the source, cancel the shadow plate. Figures stand frontally. Camera: slow drifts, a tilt up. References: Frank Newbould, Abram Games. Avoid: dot screens, clean vector edges, big saturated fields.

styles.name: 卡萨布兰卡
styles.desc: 影片本身的样子：Arthur Edeson 的片厂黑白，画成精修剧照：带眼神光的柔焦特写、百叶窗投影、烟雾里的光柱。扮里克的 Clawd 是唯一的颜色。
styles.prompt:
